title: Canonical top cohomology comparison for derived module pullback
statement:
Let $g:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $n\in\mathbf Z$, and $C\in D(\mathcal O_S)$ [def-pc-derived-category] with $H^i(C)=0$ for $i>n$. Use the canonical truncation $\tau_C:C\to H^n(C)[-n]$ of the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback], and ordinary module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. For an $\mathcal O_S$-module $M$, let $c_{g,M}:Lg^*(M[0])\to(g^*M)[0]$ be the comparison normalized as the transpose of the ordinary pullback unit [def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map]. Then $H^i(Lg^*C)=0$ for $i>n$, $H^0(c_{g,M})$ is an isomorphism, and
$$\kappa_{g,C}:H^n(Lg^*C)\xrightarrow{H^n(Lg^*\tau_C)}H^n(Lg^*(H^n(C)[-n]))\xrightarrow{H^0(c_{g,H^n(C)})}g^*H^n(C)$$
is an isomorphism (the second arrow uses the canonical shift comparison). It is natural for every morphism $u:C\to D$ between objects with cohomology zero above $n$:
$$\kappa_{g,D}H^n(Lg^*u)=g^*H^n(u)\kappa_{g,C}.$$
For every $h:T'\to T$, under the canonical derived composition isomorphism [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition] and the ordinary composition isomorphism $c^{\rm ord}_{g,h}:h^*g^*\cong(gh)^*$ [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition],
$$\kappa_{gh,C}=c^{\rm ord}_{g,h,H^n(C)}\,h^*(\kappa_{g,C})\,\kappa_{h,Lg^*C}.$$
No lower cohomological bound, flatness, quasi-coherence, or finite rank is assumed.

source.place: Tag 05TC, lemma-negative-vanishing: dual of (1) and dual of the truncation argument in the proof of (2), applied to the right-exact module pullback. The normalization, naturality and composition formulas are the agent assembly from this argument and the canonical pullback comparisons.

proof.text: Choose a strictly upper-bounded representative of C by the standard t-structure. Resolve it by the existing functorial flat replacement with the same upper bound. The bounded-above flat complex is K-flat, so the selected counit is invertible there. Tensor pullback preserves the strict bound. Transport this bound along the resolution and the representative isomorphism to obtain Lg*C in D≤n.

An additive left adjoint preserves finite colimits. On a complex strictly zero above n its nth short complex has zero outgoing differential; the homology comparison for a right-exact functor is therefore invertible. Resolve any such complex K by the flat replacement and apply naturality of the selected counit along the quasi-isomorphism. Both outer maps on Hn are invertible, so Hn of the counit at K is invertible. Apply this to the single module complex; its termwise single comparison is invertible. This gives the specified comparison on Hn for every module, in particular the asserted H0 comparison.

The Hom-set bijection defining the top projection gives its prescribed homology and naturality. Factor it through the standard truncation C→τ≥n C. The resulting map between objects concentrated in degree n is an isomorphism, since it is invertible on Hn and all other homology objects vanish. Derived pullback preserves every upper bound by the first step. Apply it to the truncation triangle; its first term is still in D≤n−1, so the long exact sequence makes Hn of the pulled-back truncation projection invertible. Compose this with the single comparison from the previous step and the canonical single/homology isomorphism to prove invertibility of κ.

Naturality of the top projection, the selected counit, the termwise single comparison, and the single/homology isomorphism gives the displayed naturality equation for every derived morphism between objects in D≤n. All equalities are proved using the Hom-set bijection, functoriality and associativity.

The section-normalized tensor adjunction equals the adjunction already selected by exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction, by uniqueness of its unit on sections. The inverse section-composition comparison is therefore exactly the underived composition mate used by the pinned derived composition. Evaluate the existing selected-counit composition equation on the single complex in degree n. Compatibility of termwise mapping with single complexes is checked in degree n by the single degree identification; the remaining components factor through zero objects. Naturality of the selected counit then gives composition of the pinned single comparisons directly in degree n, without using shifts.

For every v:C→M[-n] with C in D≤n, the Hom-set bijection gives τ_C followed by the single embedding of Hn(v) and the single/homology identification equal to v. Apply this to v=Lg*(τ_C) followed by the pinned g single comparison. Thus v factors as τ_(Lg*C) followed by the single embedding of κ_g,C. Combine the preceding single-composition equation with naturality of the pinned composition at τ_C and naturality of the h single comparison at κ_g,C. Apply Hn and the natural single/homology isomorphism. This is precisely the displayed composition equation, with the specified proof hbound.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q44-01d75847e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and all 8 steps in full, with every cited statement and Stacks 05TC lemma-negative-vanishing (derived.tex 5497ff; the item is its dual for the right-exact Lg^*). Shape: one commit, no new nodes, statement verbatim against live (live is unsplit), no repair note, not dropped, no cycle, no SGA citation. Steps 1–6 and 8 are correct. Step 1: the same-bound flat replacement plus the bounded-above flat K-flat criterion gives Lg^*=g^*P. Steps 2–3: the left adjoint preserves cokernels, so H^n(g^*P)=coker(g^*d^{n-1}), which also gives vanishing above n. Step 4: counit naturality at the resolution q shows H^0 of the normalized c is an iso. Step 5: counit naturality at the projection p with the counit-shift node gives κ=θ. Step 6: functorial truncation gives naturality. Step 8: I traced all factors and directions; no derived inverse of c is used. Edge cases checked: H^n(C)=0, shifted singles, nonflat Spec Z/2→Spec Z, unbounded below. Fault (C3/C4) in step 7: it used the square node with f′=id and claimed c_id=id 'by adjoint transpose' with no cited statement, and identified canonicalSinglePullbackMap with c without citing the node that defines it. FIX: step 7 now cites lem-pc-canonical-single-pullback-composition (the exact single-module composition equation, f=h, g=g, N=M), lem-pc-canonical-single-pullback-comparison, and lem-pc-canonical-single-adjunction-transpose (with a=id, the transpose of p is unit[0]≫u, which is exactly the normalization of c). The square node is removed from uses, proof_deps and tool_uses, and the 3 new citations are declared as tool_uses (same unit sk-thm-picard-f-representable as the square).
